title: DCVC-RT rate-control bank compressed by Mirror
hypothesis: A compact bitrate-mode coordinate can replace selected native DCVC-RT rate-control modules while preserving BD-rate, 1080p FPS and function-call/memory-I/O cost.
physical_object: DCVC-RT shared motion/temporal-context codec and native rate-control module bank.
mirror_coordinate: Bitrate-mode View m over selected rate-control modules.
logical_multiplicity: Multiple logical video quality settings without a full independent module bank.
controls: shared module with ordinary low-rank/gating control

development.selection_metric: Not run; official trained checkpoint and codec data unavailable.

storage.authority: actual coded bitstream and serialized decoder/rate-control payload bytes
paid_objects: native rate modules or Mirror codes

success_gate: Not evaluated; require matched 1080p BD-rate/FPS and call/memory-I/O audit.
blockers: No official DCVC-RT trained weights, data, or benchmark bitstreams found.
Only one third-party repository was found; its README explicitly says inference on pretrained DCVC-RT weights did not work due to dependencies.
No checkpoint files in that repository; dependencies include incompatible/legacy stack; CUDA/NVIDIA unavailable.
boundaries: Do not treat third-party implementation as native DCVC-RT result.
No 1080p FPS, BD-rate, codec call count or Mirror metrics were measured.
